The heartbeat · from Colossians 4:2–6

Keep praying, live wisely among people who don't yet believe, and let your words be gracious and ready when the opportunity arises.

Tap each word ↓

Pray comes first because everything else depends on it. Play matters because how we live either opens doors or quietly closes them. And Say is what happens when we're finally asked — the moment the first two steps were preparing us for.

Discovery One
Read it

2Never give up praying. And when you pray, keep alert and be thankful. 3Be sure to pray that God will make a way for us to spread his message and explain the mystery about Christ, even though I am in jail for doing this. 4Please pray that I will make the message as clear as possible.

Colossians 4:2–4 CEV
Discover it

Look closely — Paul doesn't just say "pray more." What three things does he actually bring into prayer here?

Tap the 3 things in the verse 0/3

Never give up praying. And when you pray, keep alert and be thankful. Be sure to pray that God will make a way for us to spread his message and explain the mystery about Christ, even though I am in jail for doing this. Please pray that I will make the message as clear as possible.

Watchfulness (staying alert, not going through the motions), thankfulness, and one very specific ask — an open door to explain the good news about Jesus clearly.

See it
Sport example · before a match

Instead of only praying…

"Help us win."

…a teen prays:

Watchful

"God, keep me alert to how I treat people today.

Wise

Help me to play fair.

Thankful

Thank you for this team.

Open door

And give me one chance to talk about you with someone."

Live it

This is the pattern behind every daily PRAY challenge — one specific, name-it prayer at a time, rather than a vague "bless everyone."

Locked in

This week

Pray for one teammate by name before you train or play.

Discovery Two
Read it

5When you are with unbelievers, always make good use of the time.

Colossians 4:5 CEV
Discover it

Paul says to be wise in how you live around people who don't yet follow Jesus, and to make the most of every opportunity you get. Ordinary, everyday actions are being watched — and they either open doors or quietly close them.

1 · Who is Paul specifically talking about how we act toward?

2 · And what does he pair "wise" with?

"Outsiders" — people who don't follow Jesus yet. And "wise" is paired with "opportunity": how you act creates chances to be a witness, or wastes them. Live a life that makes others curious.
See it
Sport example · your call

You get benched — unfairly. What do you do?

A player gets benched unfairly. Instead of sulking, they keep cheering their team on. Nobody preaches a word — but teammates notice the passion and the goodwill, and that's wisdom quietly opening a door.
Live it

The daily PLAY challenges are single, small moments of wise action — patience, generosity, fairness, encouragement — right in the middle of a game or training session.

Locked in

This week

Choose one moment to show patience under pressure.

Discovery Three
Read it

6Be pleasant and hold their interest when you speak the message. Choose your words carefully and be ready to give answers to anyone who asks questions.

Colossians 4:6 CEV
Discover it

What two qualities does Paul use to describe how we should talk to people — and what's the actual goal?

Be ______ and hold their ______ when you speak the message.

So what's the actual goal?

"Be pleasant" and "hold their interest" — kind and gracious, but never watered-down or preachy. And the goal isn't forcing a conversation, it's being ready to answer when someone actually asks.
See it
Sport example · after training

Your reply…

A friend asks, "Why are you so different?" The SAY move isn't a sermon — it's an honest, gracious answer, ready the moment the door opens.
Live it

The daily SAY challenges are about real conversations in quiet moments — maybe one on one — asking real questions, giving honest answers, offering real encouragement.

Locked in

This week

Ask one teammate how they're really doing — and really listen.

A closing thought

Pray | Play | Say isn't a technique for being a better witness — it's simply what it looks like to bring your whole self, sport included, under the direction of Jesus.

Some weeks the door opens quickly. Other weeks it may look like the door doesn't open. It might take months of quiet, faithful playing before anyone asks a single question. Both are the plan working.

Keep praying. Keep playing wisely. And when the moment comes — say something true.

Colossians 4:2–6
For leaders, coaches, chaplains & parents
Coaches
& Groups

This guide is built for individual or squad use, but it also works as a stand-alone 60–80 minute training session for a youth group, team chaplaincy, or small group.

Suggested resources: Bibles, flipchart paper and pens, and the discovery pages.

The Biblical
Foundation

Pray | Play | Say | Together takes its shape from Colossians 4:2–6, where the apostle Paul gives believers a simple, practical rhythm for living out their faith among people who don't yet follow Jesus. It works just as well on a sports field as it did in the ancient world Paul was writing to.

2Never give up praying. And when you pray, keep alert and be thankful. 3Be sure to pray that God will make a way for us to spread his message and explain the mystery about Christ, even though I am in jail for doing this. 4Please pray that I will make the message as clear as possible.

5When you are with unbelievers, always make good use of the time.

6Be pleasant and hold their interest when you speak the message. Choose your words carefully and be ready to give answers to anyone who asks questions.

Colossians 4:2–6 CEV

This guide adapts that rhythm for young athletes. It gives them a way to bring their faith and their sport together — not as two separate lives, but as one life lived with purpose, on and off the field.

Three words,
one sequence

Pray comes first because everything else depends on it. Play matters because how we live either opens doors or quietly closes them. And Say is what happens when we're finally asked — the moment the first two steps were preparing us for.

Leading a group session · step 1 of 6
Explore the Bible

Colossians 4:2–6 · 5 min

Work in pairs. Share a story of your best sporting moment, or the best moment in sport you've ever seen.

Then read Colossians 4:2–6 together.

Step 2 of 6 · small group discussion
Pray

15 min · tap a question when you've covered it

  • How many times is prayer mentioned in these verses?
  • What does Paul ask believers to pray for?
  • What does this mean for how we pray for teammates who don't yet know Jesus?
Paul references prayer in verses 2, 3, and 4 — it's clearly a priority. The focus of his prayer request is boldness and opportunity to explain the gospel clearly.
Step 3 of 6 · small group discussion
Play

15 min · tap a question when you've covered it

  • What does Paul say in these verses about how we should live and behave?
  • What does it mean to act "wisely" toward outsiders?
  • What does this mean for us as we play sport among people who don't yet believe?
Verse 5 calls believers to act wisely around people who don't yet follow Jesus. This covers both on-field and off-field behaviour — the way we live can commend Christ and create openings for conversation.
Step 4 of 6 · small group discussion
Say

15 min · tap a question when you've covered it

  • What does Paul say about proclaiming the gospel in these verses?
  • Why is it important to speak the gospel clearly, not just live it quietly?
Verses 3, 4, and 6 are key here. It's in the telling of the gospel that friends actually hear the message they need to respond to — living well opens the door, but someone still has to speak.
Step 5 of 6
Pair & share,
then pray

10 min

  • SAY: How did you hear the gospel, and who told you?
  • PLAY: Whose behaviour had the greatest influence on you becoming a follower of Christ?
  • PRAY: Identify one or two sporting friends you'd like to see come to Christ, and pray for them together.
Step 6 of 6
Conclusion &
reflection

5 min

  • What new things have you realised today?
  • How can you apply Pray | Play | Say to your life this week?
  • What will you do about this in the next day? This week?

Point the group to the teen guide's Bring it to life pages — daily challenge cards, the journal, story paths and this week's mission.
